items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I got him -- what we needed, we lost the first saxophone player, and I mentioned him to Woody, and he hired him.

ctx.x: And never did get any recognition for being the great clarinetist that he was. He was mostly known for his baritone playing, all the records he made with Bobby Hackett and in that era. I got him -- what we needed, we lost the first saxophone player, and I mentioned him to Woody, and he hired him. He was never so happy in his life; nobody had any idea that he could play lead.
